title: Hue Amazing Marathon 2026 Review: What the 2026 Race Was Like
seo_title: Hue Amazing Marathon Review: Citadel Course, Heat, Cut-offs
meta_description: Hue Amazing Marathon 2026 review: a flat course past the Imperial City and over four bridges, 31°C at the 2.30am start, a 6h30 limit and a 3:19 tenth place.
dek: What running Hue's heritage marathon was like on 30 August 2026: the flat course past the Citadel and across the Perfume River bridges, a warm, dry night, the cut-offs, how fast the field ran, and the weekend logistics.
verdict: Enter if you want a flat, generous-limit marathon through Hue's old imperial capital and can cope with a hot night. In 2026 the course ran past the Imperial City and over four bridges, the marathon had six and a half hours, and the results list 350 marathon finishers. The field was shallow: tenth place was 3:19:53 for men and 3:54:28 for women. The catch is the heat: the nearest airport recorded 31°C at the 2.30am start and 33°C by the 9am limit, despite reports of cool air. The organiser also published no route map or aid-station plan, so ask for both before race day and pace for heat.

sections.heading: The Course: Flat, Past the Citadel and Over Four Bridges
paragraphs: The start and finish were on Le Duan street, beside the Flag Tower (Ky Dai) and near the Nghenh Luong Dinh pavilion [1]. Runners began gathering there from 2.30am, in the square in front of Phu Van Lau [2].

The half and full marathons cross four bridges: Da Vien, the 125-year-old Truong Tien, the new and wide Nguyen Hoang, and Phu Xuan [2][1]. Marathoners passed the Imperial City at around 3am [2]. The route also went past Thien Mu Pagoda, where the women's marathon winner fell and got up to keep running [2], and across the square in front of Ngo Mon [2].

Tien Phong describes the course as almost flat, with the bridges as the only real test; runners told it that none of the ramps is high, but crossing them again and again wears you down [1]. No route map, aid-station plan or elevation profile was published on the registration page or in the reporting, so check the organiser's channels for the next edition's map before race day.

sections.heading: The Weather: Hot and Dry, Not Cool
paragraphs: Phu Bai airport, about 15 km south-east of the Citadel, recorded 31°C at 2.30am on race morning, with a dew point of 20°C, 52% humidity and a 7-knot wind [3]. It never cooled: 32°C at 4am, when the half marathon started, 31°C through dawn, and 33°C with 47% humidity at 8am and 9am, when the marathon limit ran out [3].

The post-race report described cool weather and a breeze off the Perfume River [2]. The airport numbers do not support that. A dew point of 20°C is dry for central Vietnam in summer, so sweat evaporates well and the air feels less heavy than the temperature suggests, but the whole marathon was run in 31°C to 33°C air. Pace and drink for heat from the start.

sections.heading: Start Times and Cut-offs
paragraphs: The limits are six and a half hours for the marathon, three and a half hours for the half, two hours for the 10 km and an hour and a quarter for the 5 km [4][5]. The results timing points to starts at 2.30am for the marathon, 4am for the half, 4.45am for the 10 km and 5.30am for the 5 km [6]; the report also put the half-marathon start at 4am [2]. That makes the marathon limit 9am and the half 7.30am. Six and a half hours is about 9:15 per km.

Aid stations close when the course closes, and anyone more than 15 minutes late for their start is not allowed to race [5]. Finishers outside the limit get no finisher items [5]. The slowest marathon finisher in the results came in at 6:26:28; the half-marathon results still list 11 runners over three and a half hours [6].

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: Japan's Shohei Miyamoto won the men's marathon in 2:44:28, ahead of Nguyen Mai Trung in 2:46:09 and Nguyen Tien Toan in 2:55:38. Le Thi Phuong won the women's race in 3:04:37, from Doan Thi Oanh in 3:07:01 and Hoang Huong Thuy in 3:29:59 [6]. The day before, Le Thi Phuong had come fourth in the sprint race at the Aqua Warriors Hue aquathlon [2].

The field thins out quickly. Only six marathoners, all men, finished inside three hours, and tenth place was 3:19:53 for men and 3:54:28 for women [6]. In the half marathon, Vu Dinh Duan won in 1:21:34 and Tran Thi Ny won the women's race in 1:33:26; tenth place was 1:29:35 for men and 1:57:27 for women [6]. The 10 km was won in 36:37 and the 5 km in 17:07 [6]. Rankings go on gun time [5]. A sub-3:20 marathoner had a real chance of a top-ten place.

sections.heading: Race-Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: The race was the second half of a weekend with the Aqua Warriors Hue aquathlon, which included a swim in the Perfume River; the two events together drew more than 5,000 athletes from 28 to 30 August [7], and many runners did both [2]. Bibs and kits were handed out at an expo in front of Nghenh Luong Dinh [1]. Kits are not posted, but you can authorise someone to collect yours [5].

Every runner got a kit bag, an event tee, nutrition and a bib; finishers got a medal and an e-certificate, and 21 km and 42 km finishers also got a finisher tee [4]. Entry went up in four price phases, from 799,000 VND for the marathon (24 April to 24 May) to 1,569,000 VND (27 July to 15 August); the 5 km ran from 399,000 to 789,000 VND [4]. Marathoners must be 18 or over, half marathoners 16 and 10 km runners 12 [4].

Fees are not refunded. You can change distance for 200,000 VND plus any price difference, or pass your entry to someone else for a 200,000 VND name-change fee, with changes allowed until 20 July in 2026 [4].

sections.heading: Should You Enter Next Year's Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if the reason you are going is Hue itself: a flat night-time course past the Citadel, Thien Mu Pagoda and the Perfume River bridges, with a generous six-and-a-half-hour limit and a small field. The race rewards a steady runner who can handle heat, and a sub-3:20 marathon was enough for the top ten in 2026.
Think twice if you want a cool morning, or a detailed course plan in advance: in 2026 the start was already 31°C, and no route map or aid-station details were published where entrants register.
The date, fees and route for the next edition had not been published when this was written.

Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's rules and registration information, the published results, reporting by Tien Phong and Thanh Nien, runners quoted in that reporting, and airport weather records.

faqs.question: What time does the Hue Amazing Marathon start?
faqs.answer: In the middle of the night. In 2026 the results timing points to a 2.30am marathon start, with the half marathon at 4am, the 10 km at 4.45am and the 5 km at 5.30am. Runners gathered from 2.30am on Le Duan street, beside the Flag Tower, and marathoners passed the Imperial City at around 3am.

faqs.question: Is the Hue Amazing Marathon course flat?
faqs.answer: Yes. Hue is almost flat, and the only climbs are bridge ramps. The half and full marathons cross the Da Vien, Truong Tien, Nguyen Hoang and Phu Xuan bridges. None is high, but runners said crossing them repeatedly wears you down. No elevation profile was published for 2026.

faqs.question: How hot is the Hue Amazing Marathon?
faqs.answer: Hot, even at night. At the 2.30am start in 2026, Phu Bai airport recorded 31°C with a dew point of 20°C and 52% humidity. It stayed at 31°C to 32°C through dawn and reached 33°C by the 9am marathon limit. The dry air helps sweat evaporate, but pace for heat.

faqs.question: What are the cut-off times at the Hue Amazing Marathon?
faqs.answer: In 2026 the marathon had six and a half hours, about 9:15 per km, so the course closed at about 9am. The half marathon had three and a half hours, the 10 km two hours and the 5 km an hour and a quarter. Anyone more than 15 minutes late for their start cannot race.

faqs.question: How fast do you need to be to place at the Hue Amazing Marathon?
faqs.answer: Not very fast. In 2026 the men's marathon was won in 2:44:28 and tenth place was 3:19:53; the women's race was won in 3:04:37 and tenth was 3:54:28. Only six runners broke three hours. In the half marathon, tenth place was 1:29:35 for men and 1:57:27 for women.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-28 about the 2026 race, run on 30 August. Replaces a short review built on one report. Weather is from Phu Bai airport METAR observations, not a forecast; the post-race report called the weather cool, which the airport data do not support, and both are given. Start times are inferred from the results timing. The organiser's figure of more than 4,500 runners is given alongside the 2,728 finishers in the published results. The men's winner is spelled as in the results (Miyamoto), not as in the press (Myamoto). No route map, aid-station plan or prize list could be found. No rating.
